# D.AI for magpie / OpenCode

Use your [D.AI](https://dai.itbug.shop) models — GPT-6, Claude, Grok, DeepSeek,
GLM and Gemini — from any agent that speaks through
[magpie](https://usemagpie.ai) or OpenCode. The same plugin exposes a read-only
catalog of D.AI image, video and audio models to Magpie's plugin-tools MCP.

One `ddsk_…` API key is one account, and magpie keeps several.

## Add it

```sh
magpie plugin add mdddj/d-ai-magpie       # from GitHub
magpie plugin add @d-ai/magpie            # from npm, once published
magpie plugin add ./sdks/d-ai-magpie      # from a folder, for development
magpie plugin login dai oauth             # sign in with a browser
magpie plugin login dai                   # or choose the API key method
magpie provider test dai                  # one tiny call per API
```

Then pick a model anywhere magpie does: `dai/claude-opus-5-5`,
`dai/gpt-6-astra`, `dai/deepseek-v4.1-flash`, …

The browser sign-in uses OAuth 2.1 authorization code with PKCE S256 and a
loopback callback on a random `127.0.0.1` port, so no fixed port is reserved and
the refresh token stays in magpie's auth store. It uses the first-party public
client `ddc_i4mhCndrFLK3LAYBaK8d` by default. The API key remains available as
the fallback; keys come from the D.AI console (`/#/apikeys`). Custom deployments
can point at another host with
`magpie plugin options @d-ai/magpie@latest '{"baseUrl":"https://dai.example"}'`
or `DAI_BASE_URL`. `plugin options` takes the installed plugin spec, not the
provider id (`dai`).

## Chat models

The live catalog currently publishes token-metered chat models, in two APIs:

| API | Models | Path |
| --- | --- | --- |
| OpenAI chat completions | `deepseek-v4.1-flash`, `deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017`, `gemini-3.8-flash`, `glm-5.3-flash`, `gpt-5.6-luna/sol/terra`, `gpt-6-astra/sol`, `gpt-6.1-sol`, `grok-4.6/4.7` | `/v1/chat/completions` |
| Anthropic Messages | `claude-fable-5`, `claude-opus-4-7`, `claude-opus-4-8`, `claude-opus-5`, `claude-opus-5-5` | `/v1/messages` |

The model list and the prices come from D.AI's public catalog on every start
(`GET /api/system/public/capability-docs`), narrowed to the models that key may
call (`GET /v1/models`), so a model you are not entitled to never shows up and a
new model appears without a plugin update. A built-in list is used when D.AI
cannot be reached while the provider is first configured.

Every model reports its context window, its output cap, its USD/1M-token prices
and its thinking levels. Image input is marked for GPT-5/6, Claude, DeepSeek and
GLM, matching the modality table used by `sdks/pi`.

A model D.AI prices at $0 on every rate also carries `free: true`, which is the
only thing magpie accepts as "this model is free" — a zero price alone does not
get the badge.

## Media catalog

The plugin registers one free, read-only Magpie tool, `media_catalog`. Add
Magpie's plugin-tools MCP server to an agent:

```sh
claude mcp add --transport http magpie-tools http://127.0.0.1:3425/mcp/magpie/tools
```

Then ask for models by kind, capability, model code or search text:

```json
{ "kind": "image", "query": "gpt-image", "limit": 10 }
{ "kind": "video", "capabilityCode": "gemini_video" }
{ "kind": "image", "capabilityCode": "midjourney", "serviceCode": "midjourney_imagine" }
{ "kind": "audio", "capabilityCode": "suno_speech", "model": "suno-speech" }
```

It reads `GET /api/system/public/gateway-models`, so it does not need an API key
and does not spend wallet balance. Each result carries the executable
`submitPath`, the optional `fetchPath`, `resultKind`, the complete parameter
schema and the public `tierRates`. Some models (Midjourney, HappyHorse, Gemini
Video and FlowMusic) have several operation variants: filter with
`serviceCode` to choose one.

The short plugin name depends on how it was installed: a folder named
`d-ai-magpie` exposes `d-ai-magpie_media_catalog`; the published
`@d-ai/magpie` package exposes `magpie_media_catalog`.

Paid generation and account-scoped job tools are intentionally not included.
Magpie's tool process does not receive the signed-in `dai` provider's API key,
so adding generation here would require a separate tool-auth design.

For a deployment with its own OAuth registration, add an `oauthClientId` option
next to `baseUrl`; the default remains the first-party
`ddc_i4mhCndrFLK3LAYBaK8d`. A custom client must register a loopback callback
for `http://127.0.0.1:<random port>/callback`, which the deployment's
authorization server accepts under RFC 8252.

## Usage

`magpie quota` shows the account behind either sign-in: the wallet balance and
pending reservation, the tier and its cycle, included USD, the API key's own
reservation and daily limits (if any), and how many calls it made today. That
comes from `GET /api/ai/account`, which accepts both a `ddsk_` API key and an
OAuth access token carrying the `media` scope. OAuth has no key envelope or
key-level daily limits; it spends the same shared wallet.

A D.AI key has no plan window — it spends the account's shared wallet — so the
card reads as a balance, not a quota window. Two keys of one account show the
same balance but their own reservations and call counts.

Free models carry their own limits, and those do show up as windows: when
`GET /api/ai/account` returns `free_quotas`, every quota becomes a window with
its used/limit counts and countdown (`30/30 次 · 22 秒后恢复`). They are marked
`aside: true` because a used-up per-model rate limit must not make magpie treat
the whole account as exhausted for the paid models.

Magpie renews OAuth access tokens before they expire through `auth.refresh`;
the rotated refresh token is written back to the same auth store. OAuth requests
send only `Authorization: Bearer <token>` and never `x-api-key`.

## Notes

- Chat models use the provider API. Image, video and audio models are separate
  gateway capabilities; `media_catalog` returns their actual submit/fetch
  paths without pretending they are chat completions. ASR is not in the public
  media gateway today; use the authenticated `/api/audio/asr/v1/transcribe`
  endpoint when a deployment enables Fun-ASR.
- The usage card needs `GET /api/ai/account` on the D.AI deployment. Against an
  older one (404) the plugin falls back to the key's call log and shows call
  counts instead of a balance.
- The plugin never rewrites request bodies. Thinking levels are offered as
  model variants, and the gateway passes `reasoning_effort` through.
- API-key requests go out with `Authorization: Bearer <key>` plus `x-api-key`;
  OAuth requests send only the bearer token. Both carry
  `x-dai-client: magpie/0.1.7`. Gateway requests also carry the stable Magpie
  session as `x-dai-session`.
